head: e19dc94f0e03c13f041bcc4e10e723fb200e5857
summary:
This merge must not go to uat as it stands (B1, blocker). After a scan of any tree with a hundred or so files, SL-040's list takes the whole window and SL-039's results list is never seen, at any window size. The whole suite passes regardless, because nothing checks that the results list is on screen (M1).

I read merge commit e19dc94, which merges uat d78635f into 396f83b; 396f83b only adds .taad records on top of 658ed6a. The builder says the merge was left uncommitted; the engine has since committed it. In `git show --cc` I read the five resolved files and the parts of uat they now sit beside: the TopLevel code-behind, Scanner.cs and TopLevelTracker's use of the store.

The textual merge is sound:
- StartScan hides the largest files and clears the top-level list.
- The ending path calls ShowFinalTopLevel before ShowOutcome/ShowProblem, and ShowLargestFiles still runs last before EndingShown.
- The report's keys survive the move to a Dictionary.
- Both hook mode families are guarded in order.
- The B-001 to B-006 renumbering keeps SL-039's L-001 to L-003 intact.
- ScanStore's raw Size/OnDisk are still read only at Scanner.cs:281; TopLevelTracker reads the charged values.

What I ran:
- Fitness: all 29 rules hold.
- `eng/dotnet.ps1 test`: 181 of 181 pass.
- WindowCases -Case All: all 24 non-network cases pass.
- HookCases H-001 and H-002: pass.
- Rules harness plants F17 to F19: as recorded.

**B1, the layout.** uat docks OutcomePanel at the top and makes TopLevelPanel the fill child. A top-docked panel is laid out at the height its contents ask for, and a 100-row list asks for all the height it is given. I measured the published merged exe with a throwaway startup hook, now deleted, applying the report's own InView test after the ending, on a tree of 6 top-level folders × 25 files:

| Window | OutcomePanel | TopLevelPanel | Results header and list on screen |
|---|---|---|---|
| 880x600 | 369.2 px | 0 px | no |
| 880x1040 | 809.2 px | 0 px | no |

The report still carries topLevel.rows=6 and the header text. With only 6 files the results list gets 40.5 px. So SL-039's design statement that the results list "has to stay after" the ending and "gets the rest of the height" is now false. Before this merge, uat's outcome panel held only the texts and a collapsed expander.

The merged tree therefore no longer matches SL-039's recorded design (docs/design/SL-039-live-results.md:64-71). SL-040's own list and the O-024 split inside the outcome panel do hold: B-003 passes.

findings.claim: In the merged window, SL-040's largest-files list pushes SL-039's results list (TopLevelPanel and TopLevelList) off the window after every real scan, at any window size. uat docks OutcomePanel at the top (MainWindow.xaml:38) and makes TopLevelPanel the last, filling child (:122). A top-docked child is laid out at its desired height. SL-040's 100-row LargestFilesList, a virtualized ListBox in the Grid's 3* row, asks for all the height it is offered, so OutcomePanel takes everything left under the pickers and TopLevelPanel gets 0 px. I measured the published merged exe (artifacts/publish, current with the merged sources) with a throwaway startup hook in %TEMP%, now deleted, reading ActualHeight and the report's own InView test at Loaded priority after the ending. The tree was 6 top-level folders × 25 non-empty files. At 880x600, OutcomePanel is 369.2 px, LargestFilesList 202.2 px and in view, TopLevelPanel 0.0 px, and TopLevelHeader and TopLevelList are not in view, even though 6 rows are bound and the report says topLevel.rows=6 with the header text 'Largest at the top of …'. At 880x1040 the same tree gives OutcomePanel 809.2 px and TopLevelPanel still 0.0 px, so enlarging or maximizing the window does not bring it back. As a control, a tree of 6 files (a 6-row largest list) gives TopLevelPanel 62.4 px and TopLevelList 40.5 px, in view. So once a scan has enough non-empty files to fill the largest-files list, which is every real drive or folder, SL-039's 'results kept after it ends' is not on screen at all. That contradicts SL-039's recorded design, 'It is the window's last child, so it gets the rest of the height … the list has to stay after it' (docs/design/SL-039-live-results.md:66-71), and the XAML comment at MainWindow.xaml:119-121. Before this merge, uat's outcome panel held only the texts and a collapsed expander, so this is a regression that the merge introduces. The builder raised the height competition as an open follow-up without measuring it. The instruction it cites for leaving the 'fixed Grid inside a DockPanel' backlog item alone is truncated in the index and cannot be read in the tree. Whatever that item is, this consequence was not measured when it was deferred.
findings.evidence: src/FsAnalyser.App/MainWindow.xaml:38 (OutcomePanel DockPanel.Dock="Top"), :44-47 (Grid, 3* row), :92 (LargestFilesList), :119-122 (TopLevelPanel as the fill child and its comment); docs/design/SL-039-live-results.md:66-71; my measurements above (880x600: TopLevelPanel 0.0; 880x1040: TopLevelPanel 0.0; 6-row control: TopLevelList 40.5 in view).
findings.fix: Make OutcomePanel and TopLevelPanel share the height below the pickers instead of letting a greedy top-docked OutcomePanel take all of it. For example, lay the two out in a Grid with star rows, with the results row collapsing when TopLevelPanel is collapsed. Or bound LargestFilesList/OutcomePanel with a MaxHeight relative to the window. Then re-run B-003, both closed and opened, to confirm O-024's split still holds, and update the TopLevelPanel comment and the SL-039 doc if the arrangement they describe changes. Where the two slices' lists go is a layout decision across both slices; if it needs choosing rather than building, it goes to design-slice.

findings.claim: No check can see that the results list is on screen after an ending, so all 24 window cases pass while it is laid out at 0 px (B1). This is the same gap M3 closed for the largest-files list. For the results list the report carries only TopLevelHeader (its text) and the topLevel block (counts of bound rows). Neither changes when TopLevelPanel is squeezed to nothing: my 880x600 run reported topLevel.rows=6 and the header text while TopLevelList was not in view. C-002 and L-001 to L-003 read those counts. L-001 and L-002 read the list mid-scan, while OutcomePanel is collapsed, so they never meet the shape. No case scans a tree with enough non-empty files to fill the largest-files list and then asserts the results list is visible after Completed or Cancel. The builder noted 'The report has no TopLevelPanel height key, so I did not measure'.
findings.evidence: src/FsAnalyser.App/WindowReport.cs (window keys: TopLevelHeader text only; topLevel counts); tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 L-001 to L-003 and C-002 (count checks only); WindowCases -Case All: 24 PASSED on the tree where TopLevelPanel measures 0 px.
findings.fix: Add TopLevelPanel {visible, actualHeight} and TopLevelList {actualHeight, inView, realizedRows} to the report, additive under schema 1 per the x:Name convention. Add a case that scans a tree with 100 or more non-empty files spread over several top-level folders and asserts, at 880x600 after a Completed ending, that LargestFilesList and TopLevelList are both inView. Assert the same again with the unreadable list opened, using the expand mode.

obligations.evidence: Still true after the merge. Scanner.cs:12 walks on the caller's thread, and :35-37 returns run.Execute() inside the using blocks. uat's TopLevelTracker runs on that same scanner thread, reads only ChargedSize/ChargedOnDisk (TopLevelTracker.cs:61-62) and publishes immutable snapshots. No other thread writes the store. Finish is at Scanner.cs:292.
Same as O-001. ShowOutcome and ShowLargestFiles still run only after the awaited scan Task (MainWindow.xaml.cs:221-228, 429).
LargestFilesTests.RanksFilesAtAnyDepthAndNeverAFolder is unchanged; 181 of 181 pass.
KeepsExactlyTheCountLargestWhenSizesTieAtTheCut is unchanged and passes.
ATreeWithNothingToRankGivesAnEmptyList passes. The window case is now B-004 (was L-004) and passed in -Case All.
AFileWithTwoNamesIsListedOnce passes.
NoRowComesFromALink passes.
RanksBySpaceOnDiskAndKeepsBothSizes passes.
EachPathIsTheFilesExactPath passes.
AStoppedScanListsOnlyWhatItRead passes. B-005 (was L-005) passed in -Case All.
B-006 (was L-006) passed in -Case All. Merged StartScan (MainWindow.xaml.cs:169-171) calls HideLargestFiles and ClearTopLevel, and ShowProblem (:489) still hides.
AFileInAFolderTheScanCouldNotReadIsNotListed passes. B-002 (was L-002) passed with its unreadable-folder caption.

B-003 (was L-003) passed in -Case All, closed and opened, with the U+D800 row 0 and 12 unreadable folders. This covers the fit inside the outcome panel only; B1 is the whole-window fit against SL-039's panel.
B-001 (was L-001) passed. The report's largestFiles* entries survive the move to a Dictionary (WindowReport.cs).
LargestFilesScaleTests is unchanged and passes.
ScanStore Size and OnDisk are still internal. The only raw readers in src are at Scanner.cs:281, and uat's TopLevelTracker uses the charged values.
The report still emits LargestFilesPanel.visible and LargestFilesList.inView, and B-001 to B-005 assert them.
MainWindow.xaml:92-97 LargestFilesList keeps HorizontalScrollBarVisibility=Disabled, the Stretch container and the wrapping path column.
B-003 plants the U+D800 file as row 0, and both of its runs exit 0 with a report.
The ShowLargestFiles caption text is unchanged, and B-002, B-003 and B-004 assert it.
largestFilesMs is still timed around the single Top call and reported.
The fitness.yaml twinned entry and its xUnit Fact are unchanged. Fitness holds all 29 rules, and plants F17 to F19 are as recorded. The F17 note now cites a stale line (see drift).
MainWindow.xaml.cs:429-431: ShowLargestFiles is called last, before OutcomePanel is made visible and EndingShown is raised.

The star-row Grid survives the merge inside OutcomePanel (MainWindow.xaml:44-78), with UnreadableList MinHeight 40 and MaxHeight 200 (:73). B-003 opened passed in my -Case All run. This holds inside the outcome panel; the panel as a whole now starves SL-039's list (B1).

cases.evidence: ATreeWithNothingToRankGivesAnEmptyList plus B-004 (renumbered from L-004), which passed.
NoRowComesFromALink asserts EntryKind.Link for all three links.
RanksBySpaceOnDiskAndKeepsBothSizes asserts the sparse file's on-disk size is ≤ 4 KiB.
EachPathIsTheFilesExactPath asserts all four name shapes.
B-006 passed in both shapes on the merged window.

B-003 feeds 100 rows, a U+D800 row 0 and 12 unreadable folders, closed and opened, and checks the fit inside the outcome panel. The merge adds a shape the matrix never had, SL-039's results panel below the outcome panel, and nothing exercises it: it measures 0 px (B1, M1).
The design marks this case material:false, and no test feeds a probed file. The deferral still holds: LargestFiles.cs is unchanged and never reads Flags.

drift: The window case IDs moved from L-001..L-006 to B-001..B-006 (declared). Obligations O-005 and O-010 to O-014 and every earlier record still cite the L- IDs for SL-040's cases, and L-001 to L-003 now mean SL-039's results-list cases. Read old SL-040 evidence through the declared mapping: L-00n is now B-00n.

eng/rules-harness/plants.json F17's note still says the plant is 'copied from Scanner.cs:267'. After uat's Scanner changes that line is elsewhere, and the raw read is now `long bytes = size - _store.Size(charged), onDiskBytes = …` at Scanner.cs:281, so the plant text no longer appears verbatim in real code. The `_store.Size(charged)` call shape it fires on still exists, and the plant still fires as recorded.

UnreadableList has MaxHeight=200 again (declared: the three-way union with uat). The XAML comment at MainWindow.xaml:39-43 says that, opened, each list 'scrolls inside its own share'. That is only true while the 2* share is under about 200 px. In a taller share, which I read from the markup and did not measure, the opened list stops at 200 px inside its row.

The builder reports leaving the merge uncommitted with MERGE_HEAD present. The branch now carries it as merge commit e19dc94 (parents 396f83b and d78635f), authored by the engine, so what was reviewed is committed history.
